newsitem.title: ITALY: ENI, Enel mull size of electricity venture float.
newsitem.headline: ENI, Enel mull size of electricity venture float.

text.p: Italian energy group ENI and electricity group Enel said on Tuesday they planned to float a stake in their new electricity production joint venture, but had not yet decided how much.
"Our intention is to float this company on the international markets as soon as possible, maybe in New York, said Franco Tato, managing director of state-owned Enel.
Enel and ENI announced plans earlier this month to set up Italy's biggest independent electricity production company to produce cut-price electricity for domestic and foreign markets.

"I don't know the percentages, but we have said from the start that the majority will not be held by the two founding partners but will be in private hands," said ENI managing director Franco Bernabe.
"We don't have pre-fixed percentages in mind," said Enel chairman Chicco Testa. "We'll see what the market's response is. We hope the shareholder base will be as broad as possible."
Enel and ENI managers addressed a parliamentary committee on details of the new joint venture.
Tato said he envisaged that Enel will have 20 percent at most.
ENI and Enel confirmed that General Electric Co of the U.S. had expressed an interest in buying a stake, but that nothing had yet been agreed.
"No deal has been done. There isn't even a letter. They've just expressed their interest," Testa said.
Tato said, however, that GE would take no active role in the joint-venture company.
Testa said it would cover at most 30 percent of the market in Italy, once Enel's distribution monopoly is ended and the market is liberalised, and added: "We hope also to sell abroad."

Tato said the business plan was still being discussed with ENI , but the companies hoped it, and flotation plans, would be ready by summer. Testa said they had not ruled out quoting the new company in Italy, but there were technical problems related to an Italian flotation at the moment.
Bernabe said investment of some five trillion lire ($3.0 billion) is planned, mostly in the national thermoelectric industry, and create many jobs.
The Treasury said it plans to sell a third tranche of ENI in late June. Enel had been due to be privatised this year but the schedule has slipped.
